news.title: How aquanauts could help save Florida’s reefs
paras: Facebook Threads X / Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Reddit Email Print It sounds idyllic. Who wouldn’t want to occupy a newly built residence in the Florida Keys, complete with its own coral garden right outside the window? The only complication is that it is 17 metres below the surface of the Atlantic Ocean.

That is not putting off Jim Brittsan, though. Brittsan is the founder and executive director of coral restoration non-profit Sustainable Ocean and Reefs (SOAR). He is also the diver who arranged the temporary coral nursery beside the residence, having brought the corals from a site where, 10 metres closer to the surface, they faced increasing environmental stress.

sport.title: November 19, 2005: The day Roger Federer scored the only double bagel in the history of the Masters Cup/ATP Fi
paras: On November 19, 2005, Roger Federer won a special tennis match. He beat Gaston Gaudio, six games to none, twice. Federer lost only three games that day. He did it in less than fifty minutes, the fastest victory in that tournament.

This match showed how powerful Federer was. He was the world's best player at that time. Winning so quickly surprised everyone, including the fans and players. It was a record that still stands in the Masters Cup. Only two other players had beaten him that year, and they were big names like Safin and Nadal.
sport.curious: What happens when a player wins every game in a championship match for moment?

sport.title: Flavio Cobolli in tears during press conference following defeat to Frances Tiafoe, ‘I’m sad’
paras: Flavio Cobolli is already out of this year’s ATP Finals, following last night’s defeat to Frances Tiafoe. This marked his first-ever appearance at this prestigious end-of-year event, and he kickstarted it with a battling loss to Daniil Medvedev.

Such a defeat was hardly worrying, and in all honesty, it felt like his campaign hinged massively on his showdown with the American superstar, as a fellow first-timer. Whether it be fatigue, pressure, or something else entirely, Cobolli completely collapsed, and despite leading by a break in the first set, he would lose it on a tiebreak, before losing the second 6-0.
sport.apply: Pressure: between points, turn away, breathe out slowly, say one word to yourself, then play fresh.

sport.title: “Indoor hard courts should not be slow”: Medvedev takes a side in the court speed debate
paras: Daniil Medvedev is all for variety in court speeds, but on one point he takes a side: indoor hard courts “should not be slow”. The Russian, speaking at the ATP Finals in Turin after his 6-2, 6-4 defeat by Carlos Alcaraz , wants them fast, “a bit like here, a bit maybe like Paris was”.

The question came from a journalist, who pointed to the debate this week, with some calling the surface too fast and others too slow. Medvedev answered by defending variety above everything else. “I think definitely, the more different surfaces we have, the better it is, because everyone likes different courts, different balls,” he said.
sport.apply: Serve: practise the toss 20 times before you hit a single serve. Steady toss, steady serve.

sport.title: What has become clear about Carlos Alcaraz after his victory against Daniil Medvedev in Turin
paras: Carlos Alcaraz continued his ATP Finals extravaganza on Wednesday afternoon, comfortably defeating Daniil Medvedev in his second group-stage match. The Spaniard beat Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 and has improved his record to 2-0 at the finals.

Alcaraz has also now collected seven victories at the ATP Finals – the joint-fifth most among active players. It was a particularly impressive victory for the 23-year-old due to the fact that he battled a left thigh issue during the match . If Alcaraz’s issue proves to be minor, only one conclusion can be drawn about his campaign so far.
